claims.locator: Spooner et al., Section 4.4 and Table 2, PDF page 5
claims.statement: Double Q-learning is evaluated as a market-making learner; default alpha is 0.001 and gamma is 0.97.
One randomly selected table chooses the next action; the other table evaluates it during the update.
The two action-value tables are combined when choosing a behavior action.

adaptations: The exact tabular Double Q update is reproduced, including seeded random selection of which table to update, but Spooner et al.'s tile coding and eligibility traces are not.

The paper's limit-order quote action, exchange order-flow simulator, reward design and empirical market data are replaced with a disclosed L1 imbalance/inventory state and unit target-position adapter.
The synthetic transition fixture is used for deterministic lifecycle verification; no empirical PnL result is attributed to either paper.
